routesElsewhere.note: An enquiry is interest, not enrolment. It creates no student record (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. Optional fields are omitted entirely rather than sent empty, and the API supplies the follow-up date where the request names none (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The mobile format, the source, the class and the follow-up date are validated by the API and arrive as errors; the plan does not test for them beforehand.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the enquiry, its reference and its first audit entry are created together or not at all. Nothing else is touched — no student record, no applicant and no account (BR-10). Where an open enquiry already exists for this child and number, the API returns that one instead of creating a second (BR-7), so a repeated run cannot produce duplicates.

operations.name: inquiry.record
operations.idempotencyKey: child_name + contact_number + session_id, which is the same triple BR-7 uses to decide an enquiry is already open
operations.purpose: Open an enquiry taken by phone, in person or at an event, with an owner and a follow-up date.

parameters.name: child_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 120 characters, as the family gave it. Never transliterated or corrected (request-language).

parameters.name: guardian_name
parameters.notes: 2 to 120 characters.

parameters.name: contact_number
parameters.notes: Registered mobile format. Mandatory — an enquiry that cannot be followed up is not an enquiry (BR-1). Digits in Eastern Arabic numerals are normalised to Latin; a number spoken as words is not converted (request-language).

parameters.name: enquiry_source
parameters.type: enum: Online form | Walk-in | Phone | WhatsApp | Referral | Social media | Newspaper | Event | Other
parameters.notes: How the enquiry actually arrived. Never Online form — that value is stamped by UC-02-01 alone and cannot be set by hand (BR-2, PR-2).

parameters.name: target_class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active class matches in this academic session (E7).

parameters.notes: The class the family is asking about, resolved from their words. Active classes in the current academic session only.

parameters.name: child_date_of_birth
parameters.notes: Only where the request states it. Never inferred from a class or an age (request-language).

parameters.name: email
parameters.notes: A secondary channel. Omit where the request does not give one.

parameters.name: location
parameters.notes: Area or locality, which feeds catchment reporting.

parameters.name: current_school
parameters.notes: Maximum 150 characters.

parameters.name: notes
parameters.notes: What the family said, in their words. Appended with author and timestamp, never overwriting (BR-5).

parameters.name: follow_up_date
parameters.notes: Only where the request names one, and never in the past (E3). Omit otherwise: the API sets one, because a blank date means the lead disappears (BR-3).

parameters.name: owner_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No staff member of that name in this branch.

parameters.notes: The staff member responsible for the follow-up. Omit unless the request names someone, in which case the API assigns the acting user.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The enquiry as opened, with the reference to quote back to the family.

fields.name: reference
fields.description: Gapless per branch and academic session, quotable to the family.

fields.name: follow_up_date
fields.description: The date set, whether given or supplied by the API (BR-3).

fields.name: owner_name
fields.description: Who is responsible for the follow-up.

fields.name: existing
fields.description: True where an open enquiry already existed for this child and number and was returned instead of a second being created (BR-7).

errors.meaning: The contact number is missing or malformed.
errors.note: Message: "Enter a valid contact number. An enquiry cannot be followed up without one."

errors.meaning: The follow-up date given is before today.
errors.note: Do not retry with today's date substituted. The date came from the request and correcting it is the actor's decision.

errors.meaning: The target class does not exist in the current academic session.
An open enquiry already holds this child name and contact number for this academic session.
errors.written: Nothing new. The existing enquiry is returned with existing true.
errors.note: Not a failure — BR-7 says the second attempt opens the first. Report the existing reference rather than announcing a new enquiry. UC-02-10 defines no E-id for it because on screen the existing enquiry simply opens; see the open question.

planningRules.rule: Never fabricate a contact number, and never proceed without one. It is the single mandatory field that makes an enquiry an enquiry (BR-1), and an enquiry recorded against a guessed number is a lead nobody can follow up.

Never set enquiry_source to Online form. That value is stamped by the family's own submission (BR-2) and setting it by hand records a lie about where the family came from, which is what the school's advertising decisions are made on.

Never set follow_up_date to today to get past a refusal, and never invent one to fill the field. Omitting it is correct and the API supplies one (BR-3); substituting one takes a decision that belongs to the person who will do the following up.

Pass the child's and guardian's names exactly as the request gave them. A name recorded here is what the family will be greeted by on the phone, and it is matched against later when the same family enquires again (BR-7).

Never re-emit the write with the failing field removed. A refused mobile number, a missing source or a class outside the session are all the API stating something about the enquiry, and an enquiry saved without them is worse than none.
Never chain a message onto this plan. Recording an enquiry sends the family nothing; telling them anything is inquiry.message, planned separately and logged as a contact.

reversal.statement: There is no delete. An enquiry recorded in error is closed as not interested through inquiry.close, which keeps it and its history (BR-8, and UC-02-11 BR-4). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

routesElsewhere.note: A refusal is a closure with a reason, not a contact outcome.
Moving an enquiry on is the School Admin's review, not a contact log.

routesElsewhere.request: open a new enquiry for this family

routesElsewhere.note: There is no capability that moves the date alone. A date moves because something happened, and BR-4 requires the channel and the outcome with it.

steps.note: One step. The enquiry is resolved from how the actor named it; the channel, the outcome and the next date all come from what they said happened.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether the enquiry is still open, and whether the date is valid, are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write. The contact log entry, the incremented attempt count, the moved follow-up date and the audit entry are written together or not at all. Earlier notes are appended to, never replaced (BR-5), so nothing already recorded can be lost by this call.

operations.name: inquiry.contact.log
operations.idempotencyKey: inquiry_id + channel + outcome + the contact timestamp, so a repeated call does not inflate the attempt count that BR-6 relies on
operations.purpose: Record a contact attempt against an enquiry with its outcome, and set the next follow-up date.

parameters.name: inquiry_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open enquiry matches, or none in this branch. Neither is reached by guessing a reference.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with child name, guardian and target class. Two families of the same name is the ordinary case here, not the exception.

parameters.notes: The enquiry, resolved from how the actor named it — a reference, the child's name, or the guardian's number. Never a reference the planner composed.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.type: enum: Phone | WhatsApp | Email | In person
parameters.notes: How the contact was made. Required with the outcome (BR-4).

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.type: enum: Reached | No answer | Wrong number | Call back later | Not interested
parameters.notes: What happened. Mandatory — recording a contact with no outcome tells the next caller nothing (BR-4).

parameters.name: next_follow_up_date
parameters.notes: Not in the past. Mandatory: a contact recorded without a next date is refused, because the lead then disappears (BR-4, E4).

parameters.name: note
parameters.notes: What the family said, in their words. Appended with author and timestamp (BR-5).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The contact as logged, and where the enquiry now stands.

fields.name: attempts
fields.description: The attempt count after this one. Drives the stale rule (BR-6).

fields.name: status
fields.description: The enquiry's status, which may have moved to Contacted or to Stale.

fields.name: became_stale
fields.description: True where this attempt took the enquiry past the configured limit and it dropped out of the daily list (BR-6).

errors.meaning: No next follow-up date was given.
errors.note: Message: "Set the next follow-up date before saving this contact." Ask for the date; do not supply one.

errors.meaning: The enquiry was closed as not interested.
errors.note: Message names the closure date. Re-opening is inquiry.reopen and is a separate decision, never chained onto this.

errors.meaning: The next follow-up date is before today.

planningRules.rule: Never log a contact for a message you also sent. inquiry.message counts as a contact attempt in its own right (UC-02-12 BR-7), and logging one alongside it makes the attempt count and the message log disagree, which is the exact thing BR-7 exists to prevent.

Read the outcome from what the request states, not from its tone. "Soch rahe hain" is Call back later; "fees zyada hai" is a note, not an outcome; "mana kar diya" is a closure and belongs to inquiry.close. Where the sentence does not settle which outcome it is, ask rather than choosing — the outcome is what the next caller reads before dialling.
Never supply next_follow_up_date yourself. The refusal in E4 is the system insisting that a person decide when to call back, and a date invented here is a commitment nobody made.

Never chain a re-open onto a contact logged against a closed enquiry. Re-opening is a judgement with its own reason and its own record (UC-02-11 BR-6), and doing it silently to make a log succeed hides that the enquiry was closed.
Put what the family said in note, not in outcome. The outcome is a fixed set the follow-up list is filtered on; the words are what the next person needs.

reversal.statement: A contact log is history and is never removed. A wrong entry is corrected by logging the truth after it, because BR-5 appends and never overwrites. The controller has no compensating call.
